newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-BJORKMAN GIVES SWEDEN TENSE WIN OVER SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BJORKMAN GIVES SWEDEN TENSE WIN OVER SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman beat South African Grant Stafford in a tense five-setter on Sunday to give favourites Sweden a 3-2 Davis Cup win and a slot in the semifinals for the sixth straight year.
Bjorkman beat Stafford 3-6 6-0 3-6 6-2 6-2 in two hours 28 minutes in his home town of Vaxjo.
Bjorkman, partnered by Nicklas Kulti, also clinched the doubles match for Sweden on Saturday, beating South African duo David Adams and Ellis Ferreira.
"After good preparation this week I really felt good," said Bjorkman, ranked 23 in the world.
Swedish vice captain Anders Jarryd said: "I did expect it would be a tough match. When it comes down to a fifth match it is always going to be a difficult match."
South African captain Danie Visser praised his players saying: "The guys don't have all that much experience yet but we are going to be tougher every year."
The tie was level 1-1 after the opening singles on Friday when Sweden's number one Thomas Enqvist beat 69th-ranked Stafford and South Africa's top player Wayne Ferreira beat Bjorkman.
Sweden took the lead on Saturday by winning the doubles but South Africa levelled the scores again earlier on Sunday when Ferreira beat Enqvist 6-4 6-4 6-4 in the first of the reverse singles.
The final contest between Bjorkman and Stafford, watched by a crowd of about 3,000 including Swedish veteran Stefan Edberg, was tight.
After the South African took the first set 6-3, Bjorkman trampled his opponent in the second to win it 6-0.
Stafford came back strongly in the third, breaking Bjorkman in the first game and going on to take the set 6-3.
Bjorkman picked up his game in the fourth to take it 6-2, and repeated the score in the fifth as Stafford started to wilt.
"He started to look a bit tired in the fifth set and I think that was the turning point," Bjorkman said. "There was a few points where he did not run at all and that definitely helped mentally."
Sweden now face Italy in the last four on September 19-21 in Sweden.
Since the World Group began in 1981, Sweden have advanced to nine finals, winning four of them, and have reached the semifinals a further three times.
They lost 3-2 to France in last year's final.
